items.rationale: 1>2 is FALSE but 3>2 is TRUE. OR needs only one TRUE test, so the result is TRUE.

Store 1 is included because the region is Nairobi. Store 2 is included because 520 is above 500. Store 3 has exactly 500, which is not above 500, and it is not in Nairobi. Store 4 fails both tests. So 2 stores are included.
The rule flags a store with either problem, so one TRUE test is enough: that is OR. AND would flag only stores with both problems and would miss many. NOT and SUM do not combine two tests this way.

OR is a function with its tests inside brackets, and text such as "Nairobi" needs double quotes. The word OR cannot sit between tests, Nairobi without quotes is read as a name, and a single test leaves out the region rule.
